key_insight: SpecFirst argues that building software from scratch is not just a coding problem, but a specification-discovery problem first. By separating behavioral specification elicitation from code synthesis, agent-based systems can better handle tasks where documentation is incomplete and the executable is the only reliable oracle.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the difficulty LLM agents face when asked to create a program from scratch using only natural-language documentation and an execute-only binary. Current approaches mix reading docs, exploring behavior, and synthesizing code in one pass, which leads to poor performance on benchmarks like ProgramBench.
method: Treat behavioral specification elicitation as a first-class step before synthesis.
Use agentic exploration of the binary to infer how the target program behaves beyond what the documentation states.
Convert discovered behavior into a clearer spec that guides downstream code generation from scratch.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this reframes program synthesis as a multi-stage process and suggests a more reliable path for building agents that can recreate software without source code. It may improve benchmark performance and make agent workflows more robust in real-world reverse-engineering or reimplementation settings.
